critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  Situation: midway through an execution with several legs already done, the observed steps showed the gripper leaving the previously highlighted target, passing on the forward side of a stick, and arriving at a new highlighted target, with the carried-in memory holding the full letter list and legs_done equal to the number of legs completed before this one. The policy wrote legs_done correctly (carried-in plus one) but issued the letter at the carried-in index, which is exactly the leg it had just watched being executed, instead of the letter at the index it had just written. This breaks SUFFICIENCY: the memory and the step contained everything needed, but the rule mapping them to a letter was misread. The instruction already has the rule 'issue demo_moves[carried-in legs_done + 1]' with a worked line; it has to be reinforced with a self-check rather than replaced. Add: the leg visible in the observed execution steps of this decision step is the leg described by demo_moves[carried-in legs_done]; it is finished and is never issued again. The letter to issue is always the next one, demo_moves[legs_done written at this step]. Before answering, verify that the letter you issue is NOT the letter that describes the movement you just watched in the observed steps (its direction and side, read the same way as in the demonstration); if it is, you have used the carried-in index and must move one further. Keep the worked line and extend it: carried-in legs_done=3 -> the observed leg was demo_moves[3] (already done) -> write legs_done=4 -> issue demo_moves[4]. No rule is removed.

refused
  Nothing is dropped outright. The single report asked for the subgoal instruction to say plainly that the leg visible in the observed steps is the one just finished and that the letter to issue is the one after it. The instruction already states this with a worked line using the very same numbers, so no new rule is missing; what is passed on is only a restatement and a self-check, not a change in meaning. No memory field was reported lacking and the annotated memory was correct at that step, so neither the annotator prompt nor the memory instruction changes.
